statement: S102 (owner review of S100: 'Reuse the shared rule-governance principles wherever scientifically and architecturally appropriate. However, user requests express goals, preferences and constraints; source documents express factual claims and observations.'). Decisions about the REQUIREMENTS a request states, under the same precedence policy as the observation semantics (knowledge_rules decide). This program concludes requirement states only, never product facts.

vocabulary.name: reading
vocabulary.meaning: a reader of the request found this bound for the requirement: reader 'local' (the request-constraint reader) or 'shared' (the quantity knowledge's bound words, also used to read documents)

vocabulary.name: space
vocabulary.meaning: the requirement is said of an available space (a cupboard, an opening): what must fit is at most its size

vocabulary.name: range_inferred
vocabulary.meaning: a bare range with no bound word: the bound is inferred from the kind (a presumption only)

vocabulary.name: stated_limit
vocabulary.meaning: a requirement stated in the request for this criterion with this value

vocabulary.name: claim
vocabulary.meaning: the evidence supports this value of this field (S100 decision predicate)

vocabulary.name: limit_conflict
vocabulary.meaning: the request states two different limits for one criterion: neither is a confirmed requirement

programs.statement: The bound of a stated requirement and conflicts between stated requirements. Two readers that disagree about a bound, or two different limits for one criterion, leave the requirement undecided: it becomes a candidate with a question, never a hard exclusion.

rules.statement: the request-constraint reader found a minimum
the request-constraint reader found a maximum
the quantity knowledge's bound words read a minimum
the quantity knowledge's bound words read a maximum
a size said of an available space is an upper limit for what must fit (convention)
a bare range of a capacity, power or duration presumes a minimum (presumption: asked, never applied)
a bare range of another kind presumes a maximum (presumption: asked, never applied)
two different limits stated for one criterion contradict each other
rules.source: S102 audit (docs/plans/s102-rule-ownership-audit.md: the last limit used to win silently)

contested.why: the two readers of the request can disagree about a bound (different word lists): the requirement is undecided and asked, never applied

history.note: S102: first request decision program (bound of a requirement, conflicting limits).
